items.title: Attachment 2 - FCS03158 - Operating Budget - Fall 2025 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment (pp. 27, 43-44)
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services

citations.finding: Attachment 2 of FCS03158 lists the unfunded integrated service package 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair', which Administration put forward for Council's consideration. Its 2026 incremental cost is $9,938K (Parks and Roads $8,298K; Community Standards $1,640K) with 35.2 FTEs, and it states a $2.11M one-time capital investment. It was on the City Council agenda of 2025-11-24, item 7.2.
citations.establishes: An Administration-authored, costed proposal to change snow and ice control service levels (SNIC prioritization in socially vulnerable areas) was placed on a Council agenda inside the window.
citations.quote: an annual ongoing operating increase of $1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts in socially vulnerable areas ... Administration is therefore putting forward this service package for Council's consideration during the Fall 2025 SOBA/SCBA.

citations.finding: The same attachment lists the unfunded standalone service package 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation', $100K ongoing in 2026 for tow services during parking bans.
citations.establishes: A second costed proposal on the same agenda that, by its own text, changes snow and ice control operations. Whether it is in scope is borderline.
citations.quote: This investment advances corporate strategy, improves service levels for snow and ice control

citations.finding: Packages 1 and 2 are labelled 'Council Directed' and 'Unfunded'. Each says it responds to a committee or Council motion, so the request did not originate with Administration.
citations.establishes: These are answers to elected members' requests. They still meet the brief's definition of an Administration proposal.

citations.finding: FCS03158 Attachment 2 includes the unfunded “Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair” service package, with a 2026 total of $9.938 million and 35.2 FTEs. The page says the package is for Council’s consideration and its amounts were updated from the earlier committee motion. The package proposes higher-priority sidewalk repair and snow clearing.
citations.establishes: One distinct snow-service package with stated new spending was included in the Fall 2025 operating budget adjustment.
citations.quote: This service package involves a $2.11 million one-time capital investment ... Administration is therefore putting forward this service package for Council's consideration during the Fall 2025 SOBA/SCBA.

citations.finding: Attachment 2, DocumentId 278877, pages 34 and 43–44, presents two distinct unfunded packages: parking-ban towing for CAD $100,000 ongoing in 2026, and improved active-pathway snow removal and sidewalk repair with CAD $9.938 million in new 2026 operating budget and CAD $2.11 million in one-time capital investment stated in its description.
citations.establishes: At least two separately presented packages propose changes connected to snow clearing and state new spending. The integrated package's operating figures conflict internally and require qualification.

citations.finding: The parking-ban package says contracted towing would remove some vehicles before blading and states CAD $100,000 of new ongoing budget in 2026.
citations.establishes: The package changes a snow-clearing support operation and meets the primary cost reading.
citations.quote: improves service levels for snow and ice control

citations.finding: The active-pathway package states CAD $1.60 million annually for snow and ice control, CAD $1.64 million for enforcement and CAD $4.59 million for sidewalk repair; its table instead shows CAD $9.938 million in total new 2026 operating budget.
citations.establishes: The package expressly changes active-pathway snow clearing and states incremental spending, though its total cost is inconsistent across sections.

citations.finding: The Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment package seeks CAD $1.777 million in 2026 to convert temporary assignments to permanent positions across several services, including snow and ice, but states no snow-specific service change.
citations.establishes: This costed workforce package should not inflate the primary snow-service proposal count without a stated change to that service.

items.title: Report - CO03513 - Snow and Ice Control Policy and Program Review

citations.finding: Report CO03513 describes the proposed 'Well Maintained City' service package, including an eight-day residential blading service and a Priority 1 Cycle Crew, at about $23.6M ongoing operating and $11.5M one-time capital. It also presents 'further optional service enhancements' with costs.
citations.establishes: Administration's costed snow service package and costed options are in a report placed before the Community and Public Services Committee.
citations.quote: The “Well Maintained City” service package outlines approximately $23.6 million annually in ongoing operating and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding

citations.finding: CO03513 states that approving the policy needs no additional budget, that resources and service levels for 2026-27 are unchanged, and that the package will be 'brought forward' at the 2027-2030 budget. On this reading the formal funding request had not yet been made on the comment date.
citations.establishes: The Well Maintained City package was presented for information rather than as a funding decision. Under the brief's definition it still counts as placed.
citations.quote: In order to approve the proposed Council Policy C409L, no additional budget is required. Administration will bring forward the “Well Maintained City” service package to Council for consideration during the 2027-2030 Budget Deliberations.

citations.finding: CO03513 states the Well Maintained City service package is proposed for the 2027-2030 budget deliberations and gives approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding. Attachment 9 describes changes to residential clearing, pathway staffing, event snow service, and accessibility resourcing.
citations.establishes: A second distinct service package proposes snow-service changes and states new spending.
citations.quote: The “Well Maintained City” service package outlines approximately $23.6 million annually in ongoing operating and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding.

citations.finding: CO03513 says no additional budget is required to approve the policy itself, while separately describing the Well Maintained City package and optional enhancements as prospective budget proposals. The policy approval is not counted as a costed snow-service proposal.
citations.establishes: The report contains a no-additional-budget policy action as well as separate prospective service proposals; they should not be conflated.
citations.quote: In order to approve the proposed Council Policy C409L, no additional budget is required.

citations.finding: CO03513 describes the Well Maintained City service package as approximately CAD $23.6 million in ongoing annual operating spending and CAD $11.5 million in one-time capital spending for seasonal services, including residential clearing and active pathways.
citations.establishes: A third package proposes changes to snow and ice control and states new spending. The figures cover a broader seasonal package, not snow clearing alone.

citations.finding: CO03513 says Well Maintained City is provided ahead of formal presentation during 2027–2030 budget deliberations; policy C409L itself needs no additional budget, and optional enhancements depend on future direction and funding.
citations.establishes: The package had been presented for information, not formally submitted for budget approval; the policy approval must not be counted as a spending approval.

items.title: Attachment 9 - CO03513 - Well Maintained City Package Summary

citations.finding: Attachment 9 restates the package at about $23.6M ongoing operating and $11.5M one-time capital and lists its winter components.
citations.establishes: The package's stated new spending, in the package's own text.
citations.quote: The package represents approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding, and is presented here for information ahead of formal presentation during 2027-2030 budget deliberations.

citations.finding: Attachment 9 describes the service package as being presented for information ahead of formal budget presentation. Its stated package cost is not accompanied by an identified approved snow-service budget and a stated increase against that baseline.
citations.establishes: The package's stated cost does not by itself establish excess over an identified approved budget under the stricter cost reading.
citations.quote: presented here for information ahead of formal presentation during 2027-2030 budget deliberations.

citations.finding: Attachment 9 describes an eight-day residential clearing window when activated, a dedicated snow and ice team for major events, and a Priority 1 active-pathway crew, within the CAD $23.6 million annual operating and CAD $11.5 million one-time capital package.
citations.establishes: The proposed package contains concrete snow-service changes and a stated package cost.

items.title: Report - CO03079 - Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair

citations.finding: No proposal in the window states the approved snow and ice budget it would add to, so the stricter cost reading fails. The only stated baseline is in CO03079 (August 2025, before the window).
citations.establishes: The approved snow and ice budget as last stated by Administration (qualification 5); it appears only outside the primary window.
citations.quote: The total budget for SNIC is $67 million/year ... rough split of 45 per cent, or approximately $30.15 million, on Active Pathways and 55 per cent, or $36.85 million, on roadways.

citations.finding: CO03079 originally presented three enhanced service options with costs, but it was considered in August 2025, before the primary reference period. The later FCS03158 package carries an updated response to the August 11 motion and is counted once, not as a second proposal.
citations.establishes: The pre-election report informs the package's history but does not add a distinct package to the primary period.
citations.quote: Options 2 to 4 require additional funding to enhance service levels in high-priority areas.

items.title: City Council agenda and minutes, November 24, 2025

citations.finding: The City Council agenda listed FCS03158 under item 7.2. Council dealt with the item on November 25, 2025, postponed it to December 1, and its December 1 minutes record the budget adjustment being approved. The agenda page does not establish its exact initial publication date; the meeting date is the latest date it could have been published.
citations.establishes: FCS03158 was on a Council agenda within the primary reference period; the related minutes establish later consideration.

citations.finding: The 2025-11-24 City Council agenda lists report FCS03158 and Attachment 2 under item 7.2; the 2025-12-01 budget agenda lists them again under item 5.2.
citations.establishes: The Fall 2025 budget documents were placed before City Council within the primary reference period.

items.title: Community and Public Services Committee - Agenda, 2026-08-31
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: The live agenda of the Community and Public Services Committee for 2026-08-31 lists item 7.1 with the CO03513 report, Attachments 9 and 10 and an Administration presentation. The brief records an Internet Archive capture of 2026-08-22 that lists the same report and attachments, which fixes publication before the comment date.
citations.establishes: The Well Maintained City package was placed on a published committee agenda by 2026-08-22.

citations.finding: The 2026-08-31 Community and Public Services Committee agenda lists CO03513, DocumentId 304803, and Attachment 9, DocumentId 304812, under item 7.1. The brief identifies an archive capture dated 2026-08-22, before the comment.
citations.establishes: The live agenda lists the package. The pre-comment publication date rests on the archive metadata supplied in the brief, which I could not verify independently.

citations.finding: In the 2025-12-01 to 12-04 budget meeting, none of the 41 operating amendments moved funding for the Improved Accessibility or Parking Ban packages. Amendment 20 (Winter/Summer positions) was withdrawn. The main motion approving revised Attachment 1 carried 11-2.
citations.establishes: Council did not fund either snow package (qualification 3). This does not bear on whether the packages were put to Council.

citations.finding: The 2025-11-24 Council meeting considered the Fall budget items and postponed them to 2025-12-01. On 2025-12-01, Council approved the revised operating adjustment 11–2; the recorded operating amendments contain no vote funding either snow-related unfunded package.
citations.establishes: The proposals were considered, but the consulted minutes do not show Council funding those two packages.

citations.finding: Council dealt with item 7.9 on September 8, 2026, as a report not selected for debate. That Council consideration occurred after the comment date.
citations.establishes: Council alone did not have CO03513 before it by the comment date; the result changes under the Council-only alternative.
citations.quote: This item was not selected for debate and was dealt with as part of item 2.2.

citations.finding: On 2026-09-08, Council approved policy C409L through the reports-not-selected-for-debate vote, moved by K. Tang and seconded by T. Parmar, 12–0. Item 7.9 records no vote funding the service packages.
citations.establishes: Council approval of a policy cannot establish that Council approved the proposed new spending.

items.title: Community and Public Services Committee minutes, August 31, 2026

citations.finding: The committee minutes record that CO03513 was dealt with on August 31, after the comment date. The committee recommended approval of the policy; a motion to bring the Well Maintained City package to Council was withdrawn. Two separate motions directed preparation of unfunded service packages for 2027-2030 deliberations. Under the required considered-by-body timing rule, the CO03513 package is not counted by August 27.
citations.establishes: The verdict changes to Partially supported under the alternative considered-by-body timing rule.
citations.quote: With the unanimous consent of Community and Public Services, Mayor A. Knack withdrew the motion.

citations.finding: The committee minutes first record presentations, questions and motions under CO03513 on 2026-08-31, four days after the comment. E. Rutherford's policy recommendation carried 5–0; A. Knack withdrew a motion to bring Well Maintained City to Council on 2026-09-08; J. Morgan's assisted-snow package request and J. Wright's school-zone package request each carried 5–0.
citations.establishes: Well Maintained City had not been considered by a body by 2026-08-27. The later motions requested future packages; they did not fund them.

items.title: On the agenda: Parking ban fines, municipal assets, brand framework

citations.finding: Media report that the 2026-01-19 committee traffic-bylaw item proposed cutting the parking-ban fine from $250 to $150, with costed early-payment options. It described no change to snow clearing service.
citations.establishes: A lead only. It suggests CS03123 is a fine change rather than a snow-service proposal.

items.title: Attachment 10 - CO03513 - Snow and Ice Enhancements - June 2026

citations.finding: Attachment 10 lists 24 snow and ice enhancements, each with an estimated ongoing and/or one-time cost. Examples: Enhanced School Zones Clearing at $2.1M ongoing; Calcium Chloride System Upgrades at $2.5M ongoing and $4.4M one-time; Contracted Windrow Pick-up at $58.6M ongoing and $60M one-time.
citations.establishes: Separately costed options, the alternative unit.

items.title: Community and Public Services Committee - Minutes, 2025-08-11, item 7.3

citations.finding: The committee motion that asked for package 1. It is a motion, not a proposal.
citations.establishes: Package 1 is Administration's answer to this motion (qualification 2).
citations.quote: That Administration prepare an unfunded service package for consideration during the 2025 Fall Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment to implement Option 3 - Moderate Changes to Cost and Service Levels ($1,430,000 capital one time and $8,070,000 operating Ongoing)

citations.finding: On 2025-11-24/25 City Council dealt with items 7.1 to 7.3 together (presentations, questions, a private session) and postponed them to 2025-12-01 (Tang/Stevenson, 12-0).
citations.establishes: Under the considered-by alternative, packages 1 and 2 were dealt with by Council before the comment date.

citations.finding: Council motions of 2026-03-17 (item 10.3, Morgan/Elliott, 11-0; item 10.4, Paquette/Rutherford, 10-0) asked for options, costs and resource implications in the policy review, including calcium chloride and a surge-capacity strategy. Item 10.3 follows the notice of motion given at the committee on 2026-01-19, item 11.1.
citations.establishes: These are the asks that CO03513's enhancements answer (qualification 2).
citations.quote: include options, risk analysis, operationalization timelines and resource implications for different or innovative operational tactics, including but not limited to calcium chloride (CaCl) application to roadways

items.title: Community and Public Services Committee agenda, August 31, 2026, archived August 22

citations.finding: The archived August 22 agenda lists CO03513 and its attachments under item 7.1, before the August 27 comment date. The published item includes the report, Attachment 9 and Attachment 10.
citations.establishes: Under the primary agenda-placement timing rule, CO03513 was put to a committee before the comment date, although the committee meeting was after it.
